name: MonarchReactionBar
title: ReactionBar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip in androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for the quick reactions
summary: The emoji reactions under a message, comment or post: a chip per emoji with its count, selected when the current person reacted, and an add button that opens the app's emoji picker or a menu of quick reactions.
whenToUse: Under messages, comments and posts where people react with emoji and see how many others did.
whenNotToUse: For a single like or upvote use a MonarchButton or a Material 3 IconToggleButton. For filters use MonarchTag with selected. For a rating use MonarchRatingPicker.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchReactionBar(reactions: List<MonarchReactionBarItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onToggle: ((emoji: String, reacted: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, size: MonarchReactionBarSize = MonarchReactionBarSize.Sm, enabled: Boolean = true, addable: Boolean = true, maxReactions: Int? = null, quickReactions: List<String> = emptyList(), addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, picker: (@Composable (onPick: (String) -> Unit, onDismiss: () -> Unit) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchReactionBarLabels = MonarchReactionBarLabels())
public class MonarchReactionBarItem(emoji: String, count: Int, reacted: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, reactedBy: String? = null)
public enum class MonarchReactionBarSize { Sm, Md }

public class MonarchReactionBarLabels(label: String? = null, reaction: ((label: String, count: Int) -> String)? = null, reactedBy: ((names: String) -> String)? = null, add: String? = null, addText: String? = null)

options.name: reactions
options.description: The reactions in display order. A count of 0 hides the chip; a repeated emoji is shown once.

options.name: onToggle
options.description: Receives the emoji and the new state when a chip is tapped, or true when an emoji is picked. Without it the bar is read-only.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm under messages and comments, Md under posts.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether chips and the add button respond.

options.name: addable
options.description: Whether an interactive bar shows the add button.

options.name: maxReactions
options.description: At most this many distinct reactions; the add button hides when the limit is reached.

options.name: quickReactions
options.description: Emoji offered in the add button's menu when no picker is given.

options.name: addIcon
options.description: The add button's icon. Without it the button shows "+".

options.name: picker
options.description: The emoji picker, composed while the add button is open: usually MonarchEmojiPicker (the system emoji picker) in a ModalBottomSheet.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the bar's name, a chip's name, the "Reacted by" text and the add button's name and text.

states.name: not reacted
states.description: A chip on the subtle background with a 1dp subtle border and the count in regular weight.

states.name: reacted
states.description: A chip in the accent's subtle fill with strong text, a 2dp accent border and a bold count; the chip is selected.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Without onToggle: chips are images, not controls, and there is no add button; nothing is drawn without reactions.

states.name: picker open
states.description: The app's picker, or a menu of the quick reactions; picking closes it.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Chips and the add button use the disabled text color and do not respond.

appearance: Chips are fully rounded. Not reacted: the subtle background, default text and the subtle border. Reacted: the accent subtle fill, accent strong text and a 2dp accent border. Disabled: the muted fill and disabled text. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web bar is a toolbar with one tab stop and arrow keys between chips; on Android each chip is a FilterChip that TalkBack reaches by swiping and a keyboard by Tab. The web opens its own emoji picker in a popover and iOS in a sheet; on Android the add button composes the picker slot, usually MonarchEmojiPicker (the AndroidX system picker) in a sheet, or, without one, a DropdownMenu of quickReactions. The web title attribute (who reacted) is read after the chip's name. Without a label a chip reads the emoji character, as on the web; iOS uses its emoji index instead. Reacted chips use the accent tone, as on the web.
accessibility: The bar is a traversal group named "Reactions".
Each interactive chip is a FilterChip named by the emoji's name and count, "thumbs up, 3 reactions"; the emoji character and the digits are not read separately.
A reacted chip is selected, and has a thicker border and a bold count, so the state does not depend on color.
Who reacted is read after the name: "Reacted by Ana and Ben".
Read-only chips are images with the same names and no selected state.
Chips and the add button have 48dp touch targets; the add button is named "Add reaction".
Chips wrap onto new rows at font scale 2.0 and follow the reading direction.
edgeCases: A chip whose count drops to 0 disappears; the app decides when that happens.
The same emoji twice in reactions is shown once, with the first item's values.
Picking an emoji the person already reacted with does nothing.
With neither a picker nor quickReactions there is no add button.
A read-only bar with no reactions draws nothing.

examples.title: Interactive
Read-only, under a post
examples.code:
MonarchReactionBar(
    reactions = listOf(
        MonarchReactionBarItem("❤️", count = 12, label = "red heart", reactedBy = "Ana, Ben and 10 others"),
        MonarchReactionBarItem("👀", count = 2, label = "eyes"),
    ),
    size = MonarchReactionBarSize.Md,
)
